text:
maria: Quick sync — ran a focused microbatch sweep to compare streaming chat vs non-streaming completions on rtx-8x1 (kernel v2.3.1). Short summary first: streaming needs smaller microbatches to keep p99 tails reasonable; completions can safely use larger mb for throughput gains. Details below.

alex: Nice. Can you drop the key numbers (p95/p99/throughput) and the config you used?

maria: Yep. Benchmark config: 3x runs, synthetic chat and completions workloads, seq_len distribution: chat ~ 50-400 (mean ~230), completions target seq 512. Command used:```
./bench --model=rwd-v2-sm --pool=rtx-8x1 --mode=streaming --mb=4 --seq-dist=chat --runs=3
```

maria: Results (median across runs):
- streaming (mb=2): p95 ~58ms, p99 ~190ms, throughput ~210 req/s
- streaming (mb=4): p95 ~72ms, p99 ~220ms, throughput ~260 req/s
- streaming (mb=8): p95 ~120ms, p99 ~460ms, throughput ~340 req/s (but p99 unacceptable)
- completions (sync, mb=8): p95 ~85ms, p99 ~240ms, throughput ~540 req/s
- completions (sync, mb=16): p95 ~110ms, p99 ~360ms, throughput ~720 req/s

maria: Observations:
- Streaming p99 balloons past mb=4 due to one tail cause: kernel selector switches to the slow generic attention kernel for sequences that cross ~1k tokens in the inference window (we have a few chat sessions that accumulate long history). That kernel has much higher tail variance.
- Completions are more uniform (fixed seq target) so batching larger gives good throughput with controlled tail.

perf-bot: Profiling summary (2145090005): top hotpaths: attention::generic_kernel (45% of tail samples), kvcache::serialize (12%), grpc-send (8%). Flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/2145090005 (trace id fff1a).

maria: KV cache behavior note: prefix hit rate for chat workload was 87% overall, but those sessions that hit the generic kernel correspond to cache miss bursts (lots of KH cache evictions due to wide user histories). When cache hit < 70% we see p99 jump 2x.

alex: So is the issue kernel mis-selection or cache thrash?

maria: It's both. Root cause chain: (1) kernel selector uses an estimated max_seq bucket based on sample mean from recent requests (buggy estimator uses mean instead of max in commit ab12c), so it sometimes picks the slow generic kernel for mixed-length microbatches; (2) when combined with a KV spill during long histories, the backend does extra memcpy/serialize work that amplifies tails.

sanjay: Oof. Can we mitigate without rollback?

maria: Short-term mitigations proposed:
- change selector policy to pick kernel by 95th percentile seq estimate (cheap fix)
- clamp streaming mb to 3 or 4 for chat routes where window growth expected
- for completions routes, increase mb to 12/16 to recover throughput
- enable an explicit fast-path kernel override for seq<1024

jen: Cost / unit-economics question: how much throughput do we lose by clamping chat to mb=4? And cost delta if we keep completions at mb=12?

maria: Rough numbers from sweep: clamping chat to mb=4 reduces throughput ~10-15% vs mb=8 but p99 drops by ~2x so SLO violations shrink a lot. For completions, moving mb 8->12 gives ~30% throughput uplift; cost per token down ~18% (because fewer kernel launches). Will share exact per-1M-token numbers in the issue.

alex: Any signal on how this affects latency-sensitive p95 for streaming? p95 was relatively stable, right?

maria: p95 moves a bit (see numbers). p95 was acceptable at mb=4 (72ms). The scary part is p99 tails that affect SLAs.

sanjay: Proposed rollout: canary kernel-selector change (95th percentile estimator) + mb clamp for chat routes behind feature flag. 1% traffic canary for 24h. If tail improves, increase to 10% then 50%.

maria: Agreed. Also add automatic fallback: if we detect seq>1024 in batch, force use old kernel for that batch and emit trace. That avoids instant regressions while selector converges.

perf-bot: Canary job created: job/mb-canary-214509 created, link: https://ci.internal/job/mb-canary-214509 (owner: maria).

jen: Please add cost tracking to the canary dashboards — want to be able to see tokens/s, GPU utilization, and estimated $/token in real time.

maria: Will add. Action items:
- maria: open runtime issue with perf traces + attach flamegraphs (ISSUE-rt-6423)
- alex: add estimator patch + unit tests
- sanjay: create canary rollout + dashboard widgets
- jen: validate cost calc and sign-off on thresholds

maria: FYI I included a short trace snippet from a bad batch:```
[trace] batch_id=0x7f3a  seq_max=1340 selector=generic_kernel runtime=478ms samples=[attention_generic:210ms, kv_serialize:90ms, grpc_send:70ms, other:108ms]
```

maria: TL;DR: For now set streaming-chat mb target=3-4 (prefer 4 if latency headroom), completions sync mb target=12 for throughput; rollout kernel-selector estimator to 1% canary with fallback.

alex: Sounds good. Will PR the estimator patch today.

sanjay: I'll schedule canary for tomorrow morning.

jen: Thanks all. Keep thread updated with canary metrics. :thumbsup:
